It is an amp to drive speakers. It takes input voltage and current and sends that into a transformer, which gets rectified (smoothed out) at 35v and sends power to the tube heaters (filaments). The inputs send an AC sine from the guitar to the grid of the 12ax7 and the signal increases. From here: an inverted AC sign is created at the plate (while the original wave is produced at the cathode). This signal comes into the Volume pot. From the pot, you now are determining how much signal gets amplified by the second half of the 12ax7. This signal goes into the grid and again inverts the AC (now back to our original sine!) and goes to the grid of the output tube. The plate current then goes through the output transformer to drive a speaker at 5ish watts, which is enough power to produce 100 + dB with an efficient speaker; and is rated as safe for 15 minutes of ear exposure in a 24 hour period! So yeah, that little thing can rip with the right speaker!
